note: Assesses United States governance strategy specifically, including the legal risks attaching to generated content, and proposes where a dedicated regulator would help.
title: Balancing Innovation and Regulation in the Age of Generative Artificial Intelligence
explain_beginner: New AI tools like ChatGPT are spreading rapidly through society, creating both exciting possibilities and serious concerns. This paper examines the legal problems these tools create, particularly around content they generate, and explores how governments should regulate them. The authors studied US law and governance approaches, then recommend creating a dedicated regulator and stronger international coordination to protect people while still allowing innovation to continue.
explain_business: Generative AI adoption is accelerating, but legal uncertainty creates business risk. This research identifies critical gaps in current US regulation of AI-generated content and recommends establishing dedicated oversight. For executives, this signals that regulatory clarity is coming, making early compliance investment prudent. The study supports the case for industry participation in developing new regulatory frameworks and suggests monitoring international coordination efforts that will shape operational requirements.
explain_practitioner: This study conducted literature review, legal doctrinal analysis, and case study examination of generative AI governance in the United States. The authors analyzed current legal frameworks and their limitations, then synthesized research on technological and ethical implications. Key finding: existing US governance strategies have significant gaps. The paper proposes establishing a dedicated regulatory body combined with harmonized international collaboration and proactive legislation to address legal risks from AI-generated content while preserving innovation capacity.
